newsitem.title: USA: U.S. DEBT FUTURES FINISH SLIGHTLY HIGHER.
newsitem.headline: U.S. DEBT FUTURES FINISH SLIGHTLY HIGHER.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended slightly higher, recovering late from session lows but down from the morning's high.
September Treasury bond futures edged up to 113-03/32 in early trading amid short-covering after Friday's steep sell-off, but buying soon dwindled and September fell to a 112-09/32 session low.
Prices bounced from their lows late in the day on a wire service interview with Federal Reserve Governor Susan Phillips, who reportedly said there may be no need for higher interest rates.
The Phillips interview stoked the idea that "interest rates are probably where the should be and there is no fear of rate hikes soon," a Eurodollar trader said.

He noted that Euro contracts edged up after the interview, but said action was very light. He noted "decent volume" on the open, but said trade slowed down to a lull until the Phillips comments perked up trade into the close.
A Treasury bond futures trader said the overall nature of the market was indecisive and said traders appeared little interested on the push to the lows ar on the late recovery.
"You just pushed it around a little," the trader said.
He said the day's gains were tentative.
"We still have the auction hanging over our heads," he said.
Traders noted that the data line-up was empty, and said the mood could remain indecisive until key U.S. data later this week.
July retail sales and producer prices will be released on Wednesday, with consumer prices on Thursday.
Traders cited some worries that July's retail sales could show a pick-up in economic activity. Sales are forecast up 0.7 percent overall and up 0.5 percent excluding autos.
At the close, September T-bonds were up 02/32 at 112-24/32, December Eurodollars were 0.015 higher at 94.00 and 10-year T-notes were up 01/32 at 108-27/32. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750))
